newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SWITZERLAND'S LOCHER MAKES FLYING START TO SEASON.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SWITZERLAND'S LOCHER MAKES FLYING START TO SEASON.

text.p: Steve Locher made a flying start to the alpine ski season to continue the Swiss domination of giant slalom by winning the opening World Cup race in Soelden on Sunday.

Locher clocked fastest times in both runs on the Rettenbach glacier piste for a winning aggregate of two minutes 03.20 seconds, to edge out compatriot and defending giant slalom champion Michael Von Gruenigen.
Von Gruenigen, who clocked a combined time of 2:03.51, won five of last winter's nine races in this discipline.

Third place went to Norway's 1994 overall World Cup champion Kjetil Andre Aamodt, who completed a fast second run to improve on a first leg ninth place under clear, blue skies at an altitude of over 3,000 metres. Austria's Hans Knaus was fourth.
But the day belonged to Locher, a 29-year-old veteran who is better-known in his home country as the man who claimed Switzerland's only medal at the 1992 Olympics when he clinched a combined bronze.
It was Locher's third career victory and second in giant slalom. His previous win in this discipline dates back to 1993 when he sensationally defeated Italy's Alberto Tomba at Alta Badia in Italy.

"This is my most important win so far," he said. "I struggled so hard over the past two years to get back to the top of the field. Last year I could not place better than fourth so this victory comes as a huge surprise.
"Beating Micheal (Von Gruenigen) was more than I ever expected. It was nice to see how Michael himself was happy that I won. We Swiss have a great team spirit at the moment and that helps all of us."
Locher added his goal was to post consistent results throughout the entire winter to gain as much confidence as possible for the world championships in Sestriere, Italy in February.

Von Gruenigen, a slalom and giant slalom bronze medallist at last February's championships in Spain's Sierra Nevada, also hopes to make the championship rostrum again. But his main goal is to defend the giant slalom World Cup.
"I am very pleased," he said. "A result in the top three is a good way to start the winter and gives me confidence that I can defend my title.
"I now have a month to prepare for the next races in America (Park City)."

It was an unsuccessful start to the winter for Norwegian overall title holder Lasse Kjus, who was the only skier to crash out of the second run when he slid halfway down the piste. He had finished a superb third in the first descent.
"I really attacked and went for it because I really wanted to make the podium," said Kjus. "But I simply risked too much. The season is still long."
Aamodt was delighted with third place and compared the result to his last giant slalom victory in 1994 in Vail, United States, when he improved on a first leg 13th to win the race.
"This result is very good for my morale, especially after all the troubles and injuries I had over the past two years," said Aamodt, who is seeking a second overall World Cup title.
The World Cup season continues with a men's and women's slalom and giant slalom in Park City, United States from November 21 to 24.
